outputs.name: 절벽 미술관
outputs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer plus precise architecture edit.
Deliverable: one polished 16:9 portfolio world-map art-direction PREVIEW, OPTION 01 "cliff museum". This is a still candidate, not production UI.
Input 1 = composition and island-purpose reference only. Its oversaturated candy pink/yellow foliage, glowing lamps and dense tiny details are REJECTED. Input 2 = preferred broad matte stone planes, restrained natural greenery and coherent soft daylight reference; do not copy its little ruin building.
Repaint input 1 into a carefully art-directed PAINTED ADVENTURE-GAME ENVIRONMENT with selective detail and credible architectural shapes. Keep the four-island arrangement and purposes: spring tree/studio upper left, summer open workshop/wheel lower left, dominant Projects upper right, winter lighthouse/harbor lower right. Preserve their relative placement and unobstructed separation. Maintain attractive clear daylight and airy blue-sky depth. This should be a tasteful production game-background painting, not a shiny miniature fantasy render.
COLOR AND MATERIAL REDIRECTION ACROSS ALL FOUR ISLANDS:
Neutral warm chalk-limestone highlights with cool slate-blue/grey-green shadows, natural moss and sage-green foliage, softly varied weathered brown timber. Moderate clear sky blue with simple large pale clouds. Stone and timber are MATTE, with NO yellow rim-light tracing every edge, no glossy specular spots, no bloom, no orange lamp glow in daylight, no gold picture frames.
Spring: old tree with grouped dusty blush blossom patches mixed with more fresh green foliage; large calm canopy shapes, no individually shiny confetti flowers.
Summer: cooler medium/deep green tree canopies, quiet broad shapes. Keep the workshop recognizably functional.
Autumn: mostly olive/sage planting with just one ochre-gold ginkgo and one soft rust-red maple beside Projects. These are small controlled accents, never fluorescent yellow or orange. Most rock is exposed, not coated in flowers and ivy.
Winter: sparse blue-green pines and bare twigs, tiny shaded frost accents, open water. Not a snow globe.
SIMPLIFY DETAIL: foliage painted as coherent masses with 2–3 major light/shadow values; rocks have large broken planes and a few chosen seams, not hundreds of tiny faceted polygons; small textures concentrated at entrances and interaction areas. Maintain strong forms and readable depth without global blur or a grey desaturation filter. Keep natural asymmetry and imperfect edges. Leave quiet unadorned surfaces.
REPLACE PROJECTS CASTLE COMPLETELY with option 01:
A MONUMENTAL ASYMMETRIC CLIFF MUSEUM carved into two massive rock shoulders. Two offset rectilinear pale stone gallery volumes, one tall recessed vertical entrance slit and one long projecting horizontal exhibition wing. A substantial broad stair rises through the rock to a deep shadowed entrance courtyard. Four large open-front exhibition bays are visible, two upper/lower on each side of the entry; exactly FOUR quiet blank matte grey-ivory display planes, unlit, with no ornate frames. This is a place to display the owner's actual design work later; never invent app screenshots, branding, posters, or paintings.
Architecture is half embedded in the cliff, thick calm wall planes and one dramatic cantilever supported convincingly; a clear large sky void separates the two rock shoulders below. Monumentality comes from big masses, deep recesses and small human-scale stairs/railings, not turrets or repetition. Few strategically placed trees. No castles, pitched palace roofs, columns in endless arcades, spires, glass shopping mall facade or spaceship.
A waterfall emerges from a credible pool inside the rock cut and drops through the central void. A shorter narrow side spill on the far edge, with soft simple water shape and restrained mist.
Other islands retain their approved building identities, repainted to the new subdued material/planting direction.
Keep ALL objects and highest roofs fully inside canvas, ample sky above. Text: retain only the four small readable unboxed labels "ABOUT", "SKILLS", "PROJECTS", "CONTACT" below respective islands, dark ink, restrained modern sans. No extra headings/numbers/UI/borders/characters/logos.

The four work surfaces are blank matte ivory plaster/unprinted display panels, deliberately awaiting actual user portfolio screenshots; no fake UI, fabricated project imagery, painting, logos, gold frames or text. No floating monitors, castle turrets, neon, portals, confetti or new characters. Exactly four clearly visible exhibition surfaces. Preserve the visual clarity of a personal portfolio destination.
Architecture to replace Projects with:
OPTION 02: MONUMENTAL TERRACED EXHIBITION GARDEN. Completely demolish the previous tall block building and the central doorway. Create an open-air fan-shaped/crescent gallery carved into THREE broad ascending curved limestone terraces, wrapping a generous open central court with a small reflecting pool. Its silhouette is low, wide and stepped rather than a tall rectangular building. Each of four exhibition bays is an independent substantial stone wall plane, two on the lower terrace and two staggered on the upper terraces, backed by short retaining walls and occasional very shallow overhangs; stagger heights and wall angles so all four blank display surfaces face the viewer. These are museum exhibition walls in a sculpture garden, not giant freestanding television screens and not rows of stadium seating. Use LARGE landscaped terrace steps, only a few small circulation stairs and credible subtle railings. No central stage and no amphitheatre audience benches. One bold curving ramp links the terraces around one outer edge. Mature olive trees and a single subdued ochre ginkgo frame the upper ridge; retain ample quiet unplanted paving. The four displays remain the main architectural rhythm. A pool on the upper terrace feeds a narrow side cascade into the central chasm waterfall beneath. Sense of grandeur comes from the wide curved spaces, deep terrace cuts and massive suspended rock base. No castle, mansion, repeated arcade or tall enclosed front facade. The garden should read immediately as a different architectural composition from option 01.
